newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African shares seen drifting, nervous next week.
newsitem.headline: S.African shares seen drifting, nervous next week.

text.p: South African shares are set to drift sideways or inch lower next week as nervousness creeps into the market, dealers and portfolio managers said on Friday.

After a strong recent surge, the Johannesburg Stock Exchange slipped back a touch this week as market participants kept a close eye on volatile New York shares and inflation fears across the Atlantic.

Such Wall Street-watching breaks the usual pattern of South African equities, but the country's much expected interest rate cut is now mostly discounted in the market, leaving fund managers in search of inspiration from overseas bourses.
But all funds have seen recently is wild price swings in New York and a general nervousness about emerging markets.

"A little nervousness is coming into the market, but I don't see any real sell-off. The market will just drift down to sideways and towards the end of the month will pick up again," said Malcolm Chapman, general manager of ABSA Asset Management.
Aside from nervous signals from Wall Street this week, South African shares were also weighed by a steep fall in leading stock De Beers Ltd .
The diamond group posted a disappointing set of half-year results on Tuesday and the market immediately began to punish its stock, dragging the all-share index down with it.
The stock, which on Tuesday was trading at 171.50 rand, was quoted around the 151 rand level by midday on Friday.
Next week the corporate scene is still heavily populated with results, but upsets are not likely to have such an effect on the broader market.
"De Beers had such an impact because it is so heavily weighted (in the indices)," said one portfolio manager who declined to be named.
On Monday Ingwe Coal Ltd is expected to post good gains in its year profits, but world coal prices are seen taming the rise.

On Thursday Wooltru Ltd is seen posting healthy half-year figures despite concerns about the effects of high interest rates on consumer spending, while on the same day foods firm Irvin & Johnson Ltd is set to lift its year profits.
However, analysts warn that I&J is coming off a low base last year.

On the economic side there are no major figures due to be released, but South Africa's largest labour body, the Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu), is holding a series of protests against planned new labour legislation.

On Monday there will be a one-day strike in Eastern Cape province, followed by similar actions on Tuesday in KwaZulu-Natal and Mpumalanga, on Wednesday in Free State and Western and Northern Cape provinces and on Thursday in Gauteng.
However, noting a muted response to Cosatu's last call for a one hour national stoppage, portfolio managers said investors were unlikely to pay too much heed to the action.
"At the moment, not a lot of attention is being focused on that," Chapman said.
